new_statements.quote: 147. Orhon Türkçesinde sözcük vurgusu, belirli istisnalar dışında, genellikle son hece üzerinde idi. [...] Üç heceli sözcüklerde, ilk hecede de ikinci derecede bir soluk vurgusu vardı; orta hece ise vurgusuzdu. [...] Eklenmede sözcük vurgusu son heceye kayıyordu: bodún "halk", bodunúm "halkım", bodunumín "halkımı", vb. Ancak, belirli ekler vurguyu üzerlerine çekmiyor, vurgu ekten önceki hece üzerinde kalıyordu: bírmädi "vermedi", udímatı "uyumayarak", kılínmadok "yaratılmamış", bíliŋ "bilin!", ánın "onun ile", ókun "ok ile", kaganímın "hakanımla birlikte", ótça "ateş gibi", vb.
new_statements.translation: 147. In Orkhon Turkic, word stress, apart from certain exceptions, was generally on the last syllable. [...] In trisyllabic words there was also a secondary expiratory stress on the first syllable; the middle syllable was unstressed. [...] Under suffixation the word stress shifted to the last syllable: bodún 'people', bodunúm 'my people', bodunumín 'my people (acc.)', etc. However, certain suffixes did not attract the stress; the stress remained on the syllable before the suffix: bírmädi 'did not give', udímatı 'without sleeping', kılínmadok 'not created', bíliŋ 'know!', ánın 'with that', ókun 'with an arrow', kaganímın 'together with my kagan', ótça 'like fire', etc.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog holds Old Turkic with an empty rule; this supplies the rule (final stress with unstressable suffixes, initial secondary stress). Describes Orkhon (runic-inscription) Turkic specifically.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default stress on the last syllable of the word, moving rightward onto added suffixes; a closed class of suffixes (negative -mA-, imperative -(X)ŋ, converb -mAtI, participle -mAdOk, instrumental +(X)n, equative +čA, comitative +(X)n) is unstressable and leaves stress on the preceding syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary ('ikinci derecede bir soluk vurgusu') on the first syllable of trisyllabic words; the middle syllable is unstressed, which is why its short high vowel syncopates (adríl- < *adırıl-).
new_statements.exceptions: Pre-stressing suffixes: negation (bírmädi), converb -mAtI (udímatı), -mAdOk (kılínmadok), imperative (bíliŋ), instrumental/comitative +(X)n (ánın, ókun, kaganímın), equative +čA (ótça). Evidence cited: vowel alternations occur mainly outside the final syllable (alpagú ~ yılpagút, ärsä́r ~ irsä́r).
new_statements.identity_note: Tekin 1968/2003 and Kononov 1980 describe the Orkhon (runic-inscription) variety of Old Turkic, 8th-9th c; Gabain 1950 describes Old Uyghur (the manuscript language) and her par. 13 speaks of 'das Uigurische'; Erdal 2004 covers Old Turkic as a whole (Orkhon, Uyghur, Qarakhanid examples). Glottolog files all these under oldu1238 (hh.bib language code 'Old Turkic = Old Turkish = Old Uighur [oui]'); the bookkeeping languoid oldt1247 was checked separately on 2026-09-17.

new_statements.quote: 13. Ob das Uigurische Druck- und musikalischen Akzent gehabt hat, ist noch unklar. Die offne Mittelsilbe war jedenfalls schwach. Das Vorhandensein von stabreimender Poesie und von Wort-Kompositionen wie qap-qara „ganz schwarz“ läßt auf ein gewisses Herrschen der Anfangssilbe über die Endsilbe schließen. Dazu stimmt die Tatsache, daß sich die Vokalharmonie nach der ersten Silbe richtet.
new_statements.translation: 13. Whether Uyghur had dynamic (expiratory) and musical accent is still unclear. The open medial syllable was in any case weak. The existence of alliterative poetry and of word compounds such as qap-qara 'completely black' suggests a certain dominance of the initial syllable over the final syllable. This agrees with the fact that vowel harmony is governed by the first syllable.

new_statements.quote: § 85. В ТРП ударение было, по-видимому, экспираторным и падало, как правило, на последний слог двусложного слова. В трехсложных и четырехсложных словах возникает вторичное ударение, падающее на первый слог: bòdunumín 'мой народ' (вин. п.). Средний узкий гласный трехсложного слова, состоящего из корневой и аффиксальной морфем, находящийся между вторичным и главным ударениями, часто полностью элизируется: jaŋïl- 'ошибаться' > jaŋlïš 'ошибка'. [p. 75:] Повелительное наклонение и отрицательная форма имеют ударение на первом слоге: bíliŋ (M 33) 'знай же!'; bírmädi 'не отдал'. Некоторые аффиксы не имеют ударения: óqun (инстр. п.) 'стрелою' (Ktb 33); ótča (Ktb 37) 'подобно огню'.
new_statements.translation: § 85. In the language of the Turkic runic monuments the stress was apparently expiratory and fell, as a rule, on the last syllable of a disyllabic word. In trisyllabic and quadrisyllabic words a secondary stress arises, falling on the first syllable: bòdunumín 'my people' (acc.). The medial narrow vowel of a trisyllabic word consisting of root and affix morphemes, standing between the secondary and the main stress, is often completely elided: jaŋïl- 'to err' > jaŋlïš 'error'. [p. 75:] The imperative mood and the negative form have stress on the first syllable: bíliŋ (M 33) 'know!'; bírmädi 'did not give'. Some affixes have no stress: óqun (instr.) 'with an arrow' (Ktb 33); ótča (Ktb 37) 'like fire'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Expiratory stress on the last syllable of the word (stated for disyllables, with the main stress remaining final in longer words), plus a secondary stress on the first syllable of words of three or more syllables; imperatives and negated verbs are stressed on the first syllable, and the instrumental and equative suffixes are unstressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first syllable of tri- and quadrisyllabic words; the high vowel between secondary and main stress elides (jaŋïl- > jaŋlïš).
new_statements.exceptions: Imperative and negative verb forms stressed on the first syllable (bíliŋ, bírmädi); instrumental +(X)n and equative +čA unstressed (óqun, ótča). The secondary-stress mark on the first o of bòdunumín is read from a 130-dpi render; the diacritic shape is approximate.
new_statements.identity_note: Tekin 1968/2003 and Kononov 1980 describe the Orkhon (runic-inscription) variety of Old Turkic, 8th-9th c; Gabain 1950 describes Old Uyghur (the manuscript language) and her par. 13 speaks of 'das Uigurische'; Erdal 2004 covers Old Turkic as a whole (Orkhon, Uyghur, Qarakhanid examples). new_statements.rule_in_words: Erdal assumes, with explicit caution, a modern-Turkic-type system: default stress on the last syllable; first-syllable stress in expressive reduplicated adjectives and the pronominal stem ka+; the negation suffix -mA- is pre-stressing; instrumental and equative suffixes (adverbial) probably unstressed; the syncopation of medial vowels (p. 97) shows first and last syllables had prominence over medial ones.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not named as such; p. 97 infers that 'the first and the last syllable of a word had some prominence over the others, or that medial vowels were not stressed.'
new_statements.exceptions: Expressive reduplication and ka+ pronouns (initial stress); pre-stressing -mA-; instrumental/equative suffixes unstressed; p. 242: -mAz is stressed unlike other -mA- forms, but 'we know nothing certain about stress in Old Turkic'.
new_statements.identity_note: Tekin 1968/2003 and Kononov 1980 describe the Orkhon (runic-inscription) variety of Old Turkic, 8th-9th c; Gabain 1950 describes Old Uyghur (the manuscript language) and her par. 13 speaks of 'das Uigurische'; Erdal 2004 covers Old Turkic as a whole (Orkhon, Uyghur, Qarakhanid examples). readall_conflicts: The two listed works (both the same archive.org record of Tekin 1968) could not be opened (print-disabled, not reachable by automated download), so nothing was read from the listed works themselves. Among the on-disk substitutes, Tekin 2003 (the author's Turkish revised edition of Tekin 1968), Kononov 1980 and Erdal 2004 agree: default final stress in Orkhon/Old Turkic, with unstressable suffixes (negative -mA-, imperative, instrumental +(X)n, equative +čA) leaving stress on the preceding syllable, and a secondary stress on the initial syllable of longer words. Gabain 1950 (par. 13, on Old Uyghur) disagrees in stance rather than in placement: she says it is 'noch unklar' whether the language had dynamic or musical accent at all, and reads alliteration, qap-qara-type reduplication and vowel harmony as hinting at initial-syllable dominance; Erdal (p. 242) likewise warns that 'we know nothing certain about stress in Old Turkic'. Menges 1995 and Clauson 1962 (read in the 2026-09-17 oldt1247 check, not re-read here) give only comparative remarks, no Old Turkic rule.

Dazu stimmt die Tatsache, daß sich die Vokalharmonie nach der ersten Silbe richtet.' Sec. 15 'Vokal-Reduktion' (pp. 43-44) adds that the vowel of a medial open syllable was weak and could sporadically drop (oγulï ~ oγlï).
sources.note: Second primary grammar with an explicit accent paragraph: 'noch unklar', medial open syllable weak, alliteration and qap-qara reduplication suggest initial-syllable dominance -- independent corroboration of not determinable and a counter-lean to Erdal's final-default conjecture; worth adding to 'sources'.
